title: The Edge of Winter
subtitle: Conclusion of Phase IV and the German military situation before the renewed offensive toward Moscow.
author: R.G. Cruise
summary: The front on 14 November reveals German operational strain, continued Soviet resistance and preparations for another offensive.
outlineTopics: Army Group North's position.
The continuing blockade of Leningrad.
The operational consequences of the German capture of Tikhvin.
Soviet counteroffensive preparations and actions in the Tikhvin sector.
Army Group Center's position in front of Moscow.
The consequences of the Vyazma–Bryansk encirclements.
The status of the Mozhaisk defensive sectors.
The continued Soviet defense of Tula.
The condition of German armored formations.
German supply, fuel, ammunition, and repair problems.
The effects of autumn weather and changing ground conditions.
Soviet reserve formations and military reorganization.
The November 7 military parade in Moscow and its political significance.
The Soviet military and industrial evacuation effort.
Army Group South's position in eastern Ukraine.
The continuing German advance toward Rostov.
The military situation in Crimea and around Sevastopol.
Soviet resistance in the southern theater.
The continuing consequences of the Romanian occupation of Odessa.
The expansion of occupation violence, forced labor, persecution, and mass murder.
German operational expectations for the approaching winter.
The changing balance between German offensive capacity and Soviet defensive strength.
The decisions and preparations leading to the renewed German offensive beginning in mid-November.
researchStatus: Research brief. Full study and dated military reconstruction in preparation.
referenceMapStatus: Candidate 12 November situation sheet for background only; no 14 November sheet is identified in the supplied sequence.
chronologyNotes: The supplied Library of Congress sequence has a 12 November sheet, but no sheet dated 14 November. Do not relabel the earlier map or depict movements from 15 November onward as complete.
